title: Functionalization of clay surface for the removal of uranium from water
author: Bao, Guo, et al.

steps.title: Weigh clay sample
steps.instruction: Weigh about 0.10 g of the selected clay mineral into a clean beaker.

steps.title: Add phosphoric acid
steps.instruction: Add enough 1.0 mol L⁻¹ phosphoric acid solution to fully wet the clay in the beaker.

steps.title: Shake acid‑treated mixture
steps.instruction: Place the beaker on a shaker and agitate at 100 rpm at room temperature for 1 hour.

steps.title: Equilibrate after acid treatment
steps.instruction: Allow the acid‑treated clay to stand at room temperature for an additional 1 hour.

steps.title: Separate acid solution
steps.instruction: Separate the liquid phase from the phosphoric‑acid‑adsorbed clay (e.g., decant or filter).

steps.title: Add uranium solution
steps.instruction: Add a uranium solution of 200 mg L⁻¹ concentration to the clay sample.

steps.title: Shake uranium adsorption
steps.instruction: Return the beaker to the shaker and mix at 100 rpm at room temperature for 1 hour.

steps.title: Equilibrate and centrifuge
steps.instruction: Let the mixture equilibrate at room temperature for 1 hour, then centrifuge and collect the supernatant.

steps.title: Measure uranium concentration
steps.instruction: Analyze the collected supernatant for uranium concentration using ICP‑MS.

steps.title: Dry sample and record FTIR
steps.instruction: Dry the remaining clay in an oven at 110 °C, then acquire its FTIR spectrum.
